paper_title: dKV-Cache The Cache for Diffusion Language Models
caption: Impact of batch size on decoding speed. Evaluated on LLaDA with a single NVIDIA H20; prefill length fixed at 100 tokens.
model_annotation: The diagram illustrates the relationship between batch size and decoding speed, measured in tokens per second, for various sequence lengths (L). The x-axis represents batch size, ranging from 0 to 120, with tick labels at regular intervals of 20. The y-axis represents tokens per second, ranging from 0 to 225, with tick labels at intervals of 25. The diagram features four solid lines and four dashed lines, each representing a different sequence length (L) of 16, 32, 64, and 128. For L = 16, the solid line starts at approximately 34.93 tokens/s and increases to 202.31 tokens/s, while the dashed line starts at 35.02 tokens/s and remains relatively constant around 35 tokens/s. For L = 32, the solid line starts at 46.69 tokens/s and increases to 183.28 tokens/s, while the dashed line starts at 48.93 tokens/s and remains relatively constant around 48-49 tokens/s. For L = 64, the solid line starts at 67.19 tokens/s and increases to 175.85 tokens/s, while the dashed line starts at 54.43 tokens/s and remains relatively constant around 54-55 tokens/s. For L = 128, the solid line starts at 110.55 tokens/s and increases to 130.58 tokens/s, while the dashed line starts at 58.61 tokens/s and remains relatively constant around 58-59 tokens/s.
